newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Royal&Sun H1 weighed down by winter.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Royal&Sun H1 weighed down by winter.

text.p: Royal & Sun Alliance, the newly merged and largest British composite insurer, was expected next Thursday to report lower interim profits than the two companies together did a year ago, mainly due to the effect of fierce winter weather in the northern hemisphere.
Analysts' forecasts for first half pre-tax operating profits excluding merger costs ranged from 350 million to 435 million stg compared with 473 million a year ago.
Royal & Sun was expected to report an underwriting loss in the UK, weighed down by falling rates, higher numbers of claims and a particularly fierce winter in Britain and the U.S.

The two merged in July, creating a company with market capitalisation of 5.4 billion stg. Senior executives of the new group said in May when they announced the merger, there would be cost savings of around 175 million stg annually from 1998.
Royal & Sun at the end of July said it would close 94 branch offices with the loss of around 300 jobs. It is expected to shed around 4,000 staff in the UK as part of a wider review.
The market will look for further details of rationalisation and for how much the result is affected by subsidence claims in the UK, where the group has a relatively high exposure.
